title: Root Cause
description: Finds the smallest slice of the business that explains the largest part of a change — searching every dimension and combination, not just the obvious one.
noProjectHint: Root-cause analysis runs against one project's saved data. Choose a project in the sidebar.
optionsFailed: Could not read this project's data
includeWeekdayHint: Off by default: two periods rarely contain the same number of each weekday, so a weekday can appear to explain a change the calendar caused.
maxDepthHint: How many conditions may be combined — 3 finds 'product × region × channel'.
beamWidthHint: How many slices are expanded per level. Wider is more thorough and slower; half the beam follows the biggest slices, half the most anomalous.
minEpHint: A slice must account for at least this much of the total change to be reported.
minSignalHint: How far a slice's move must exceed its own sampling noise. Set to off to see everything, including random swings.
searchingStage: Evaluating slices across every dimension combination…
emptyBody: Choose a metric and a comparison, then run the search. It evaluates every combination of dimensions that could matter and ranks what it finds.
cannotAnswer: This cannot be answered from the data
liftHint: Share of the change divided by share of the rows. 10× means the slice carried ten times its own weight.
vsExpectedHint: How far it missed the business-wide rate. Had it merely tracked the company trend it would have been {expected}. A slice that moved at exactly the company rate contributed a lot and caused nothing.
restOfBusinessHint: How the rest of the business moved over the same period. Near zero is what licenses the sentence 'everything else is flat'.
signalHint: How many standard errors the slice's excess clears, allowing for both how many transactions it has and how much they vary.
leadTooltip: Real, but it does not clear {z}σ — the bar once every slice tested in this run is accounted for. Worth checking, not worth acting on yet.
bridgeSentence: The change here is driven by {driver}: {volume} from order count versus {basket} from order size ({orders} orders).
noSliceTitle: The change is spread, not concentrated
noSliceBody: No single slice accounts for enough of the change while clearly exceeding its own noise. That is itself the finding — this is a broad move, not a segment failure.
drillPathHint: Each added condition, and how much it sharpened the explanation (share of change / share of rows).
perDimensionHint: One dimension at a time. The dimension needing the fewest values to explain two thirds of the change is usually the one worth drilling into.
searchStatsHint: Published rather than summarised: a drill-down that quietly stopped early would present a partial answer as a complete one.
